summary: The Cambridge Trust Global South Trailblazer Scholarship is a new doctoral award at the University of Cambridge for applicants whose primary nationality is one of the 134 member states of the UN's largest coalition of developing countries (the Global South). The research must support the sustainable development of the Global South under one of five themes. There is no separate scholarship application. The award pays tuition and College fees, annual maintenance, the student visa and the Immigration Health Surcharge, plus further unnamed benefits; about 8 awards are listed for 2027/28.
eligibility_notes:
For PhD applicants whose primary nationality is one of the 134 member states of the UN's largest coalition of developing countries, called the Global South. Overseas (international) fee status is required. The scholarship applies to 114 courses and can be held full-time or part-time.

The research must support the sustainable development of the Global South under one of five themes: Energy and infrastructure; Global health solutions; AI, data and digital innovation; Governance, policy and systems; Human identity and culture. The pages name the themes but do not describe them further.

The pages read do not print the country list; the list is linked on the funding listing but did not open. The listing gives financial need (including hardship) and academic merit as the basis of award. You need a conditional offer of admission. Cambridge's minimum for entry is a 2:1 UK Bachelor's degree or an international equivalent, and many courses ask for more. No funding is given for a degree at the same level as, or lower than, one you already hold (a required second MPhil before PhD is an exception), and students part-way through a Cambridge course cannot apply unless they apply for a higher degree after graduating.

Language: if English is not your first language, your course may need a test; see the requirements list.
age_experience_notes: No age limit or work-experience requirement is stated. The Trust says applicants are not treated less favourably because of age.
funding_summary: The scholarship covers the University tuition fee at the international rate, the College fee, annual maintenance described as sufficient for a single person, the student visa and the Student Immigration Health Surcharge, plus "various additional benefits" that are not itemised. The Trust will, on application, give up to a further 6 months of maintenance to help write up the PhD. The standard length of funding is not stated on the pages read; the Trust gives no extension funding beyond 3.5 years.
programmes_note: Doctoral study whose research relates to one of five Global South themes: Energy and infrastructure; Global health solutions; AI, data and digital innovation; Governance, policy and systems; Human identity and culture. The listing says 114 courses are covered; the list is linked but did not open in the page text.
institutions_note: University of Cambridge only. The scholarship can be held at any Cambridge College. On the application you may name up to two Colleges or leave it blank; the Trust does not choose the College or arrange accommodation.

summary.detail: PhD, full-time or part-time, on any of 114 courses. Research must fit one of the five Global South themes. About 8 awards for 2027/28. Up to a further 6 months of maintenance for writing up, on application.

benefits.limit_text: University tuition fee at the international rate, and the College fee
Annual maintenance sufficient for a single person (no amount is given on the pages read)
benefits.conditions: The Trust will, on application, give up to a further 6 months of maintenance to write up the PhD; no funding beyond 3.5 years. The Trust generally gives no allowance for spouses, children or dependants.

Listed on the scholarship page. The Trust's guidance for awardees says most scholars pay their own visa and Immigration Health Surcharge and that the offer letter states whether the Trust covers them, so check the offer letter.
Listed on the scholarship page; see the visa note above.
Not described on the scholarship page or the funding listing.

benefits.limit_text: Travel is paid only if the offer letter says so
benefits.conditions: Scholars otherwise arrange and pay for their own travel and accommodation.

benefits.limit_text: Additional funding for current scholars on request
benefits.conditions: Extension of maintenance (PhD, up to 6 months, apply no later than one month before the award ends); hardship funding for unforeseen events; conference funding of up to GBP 500 for PhD scholars on a full scholarship, with supervisor approval. Not paid: childcare and dependant costs, direct research costs, private medical expenses. The Trust does not pay for pre-sessional language courses.

requirements.text: Cambridge postgraduate admissions application (PhD) submitted through the Applicant Portal by your course's funding deadline, with the funding section completed to say you wish to be considered for funding. The funding listing says there are additional questions to answer in the Applicant Portal for this scholarship. A conditional offer of admission is needed. Each course needs its own application. Agents' applications are not accepted. The application must be in English and Latin script.

Research proposal giving the topic, how it extends existing work, why it matters and why it is feasible in the time and resources available. It must show that the research supports sustainable development of the Global South under one of the five themes. A separate proposal is needed for each course.

Declare significant income from all sources (salaries, business profit, rents, dividends) in the funding section; the Trust says many awards need evidence of financial need, and the listing names financial need as a basis for this scholarship.

Academic transcripts and certificates for every degree you have taken. If you are still studying, an interim or unofficial transcript is accepted and the final one is needed after an offer. Upload scanned originals; originals may be checked later through a verification service.

Two referees, entered in the Applicant Portal. They upload references in English through the Referee Portal by the application deadline; email and post are not accepted. Referees should be academic or professional depending on how long ago you left higher education (two academic referees if you are studying or left within 3 years). Do not name PhD students.
Curriculum vitae or resume, uploaded with the application.
Personal statement describing your skills, experience, academic achievements and motivation for the course.

English test result (IELTS Academic, IELTS for UKVI Academic, IELTS One Skill Retake, IELTS Online, TOEFL iBT including Home Edition, or C1 Advanced / C2 Proficiency for some courses). Scores come from the course page. Results must be dated no more than 2 years before the course starts. Test reports sent directly by IELTS or TOEFL are not accepted, and scores from different certificates cannot be combined.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only if English is not your first language and not exempt (exemptions apply to nationals educated in a majority English-speaking country, or graduates of a 3-year UK-equivalent degree from such a country, excluding Canada). For most courses evidence is needed only after an offer.

requirements.text: Non-English documents must come with a full translation by a registered translator; do not translate them yourself. Upload PDFs under 2MB, not encrypted. Hard copies are not accepted.
Written work samples for courses that ask for them. GRE only if the course page says it is required; GMAT is not accepted by any course.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only if the course page asks

requirements.text: Latest passport and any current or previous UK visas, uploaded to the Self-Service account after an offer so that the University can prepare the Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies.
requirements.conditional_rule: After an offer, for applicants who need a student visa

requirements.text: Application fee: GBP 20 per applicant for doctoral courses (up to 7 applications per entry year), paid by Visa or MasterCard before submitting; a fee waiver may apply. The Trust cannot help with fees or waivers.

application_steps.title: Check nationality, theme fit and your PhD course
application_steps.detail: Confirm that your primary nationality is one of the 134 Global South member states and that your planned research fits one of the five themes. Pick a PhD course in the Cambridge postgraduate directory and note its funding deadline. The main University funding deadlines for 2027/28 entry are 8 December 2026 and 6 January 2027; your course may differ. The complete application, including references, must be in by 23:59 GMT on the deadline.

application_steps.title: Check the Trust's rules and name up to two Colleges
application_steps.detail: Read the Trust's eligibility rules. You may name up to two Colleges or leave it blank; the Trust does not select the College. Apply for every scholarship that suits you, because funding is highly competitive.

application_steps.title: Submit the admissions application and answer the funding questions
application_steps.detail: In the Applicant Portal fill every section, upload your documents, pay the fee and tick that you wish to apply for funding. Answer the additional Trailblazer questions in the portal and declare significant income. No separate scholarship form is needed. The Trust cannot add information after you submit.

application_steps.title: Department assesses your admission application
application_steps.detail: The department or faculty reviews your application, may interview you and recommends admission. The Degree Committee approves (about 10 days) and the Postgraduate Admissions Office issues a conditional offer (about 10 days, longer at peak times). Admission offers start from November at the earliest.

application_steps.title: Trust selects scholars on need and merit
application_steps.detail: The funding listing gives the basis of award as financial need (including hardship) and academic merit, and the research must meet one of the five themes. The Trust does not take part in admission or College choice. The awarding period runs from mid-February to the end of July; most awards are made in February and March, and partner awards that involve interviews are often decided April to June.

application_steps.title: Wait for the offer; no news by end of July means unsuccessful
application_steps.detail: The Trust gives no updates on individual applications and will say on its website when main offers are finished. Awards not taken up are reallocated, so you stay under consideration until the end of July. If you have not heard by then, assume you were unsuccessful. Unsuccessful applicants are not notified and get no individual feedback.

application_steps.title: Return the response form and meet admission conditions
application_steps.detail: Read the offer letter and keep a copy; it may serve as proof of funding for a student visa. Return the response form before its deadline, because the scholarship is not final until the Trust has it. Meet all admission conditions on time (for an October start, the conditions deadline is 31 July) and accept the admission offer in the Self-Service account.

application_steps.title: Arrange visa, travel and arrival
application_steps.detail: Obtain a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies from the University (expected in June for an October start) and apply for the student visa, with ATAS clearance if your course needs it. The University also notes that the UK has paused new student visa applications from nationals of Afghanistan, Cameroon, Myanmar and Sudan. Plan your own accommodation and travel unless your offer letter says otherwise.

application_steps.title: Keep the Trust informed during the award
application_steps.detail: Scholarships must be taken up in the year awarded and usually cannot be deferred. PhD scholars who want to start after 1 October need agreement from their supervisor, department and the Student Registry. Tell the Trust about any other funding offered before or during the award. Extension, hardship and conference funding can be requested on forms.
